title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes mellitus.

HPI
The patient is a 58-year-old male presenting today for a routine follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes. He reports that he has been taking an oral hypoglycemic medication consistently for the past year. He reports feeling well and denies any acute concerns or symptoms. He currently manages his condition without complications.

Medication List
Metformin 500mg daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears in no acute distress. Skin is intact with no notable lesions. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: The patient is stable and currently managed with oral medications. He presents without complications at this time.

Plan
1. Continue current medication of metformin 500mg daily.
2. Patient instructed to monitor blood glucose levels at home.
3. Return to clinic in 3 months for follow-up and laboratory work.
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
